preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10000 for x in stdin.split())
preconditions.description: Input consists of exactly two integers n and k, where 1 ≤ n ≤ 10000 and 1 ≤ k ≤ 100.
Input line contains exactly two space-separated integers.

postconditions.description: First line of output is a single integer m (minimal possible) representing the smallest upper bound for integers used in the sets.
Output contains exactly n + 1 lines: first line is m, followed by n lines of sets.
Each of the n subsequent lines contains exactly four distinct integers representing a set.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= int(stdout.strip().splitlines()[0]) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:] for x in line.split())
postconditions.description: All integers in the sets are within the range [1, m], where m is the first line of output.

postconditions.expression: all(all(int(x) != int(y) for x in line.split() for y in line.split() if x != y) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: Each set contains four distinct integers.

postconditions.expression: all(all(gcd(int(x), int(y)) == k for x in line.split() for y in line.split() if x != y) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: For every pair of distinct elements in each set, their gcd equals k.

postconditions.expression: all(all(int(x) not in set.union({int(y) for y in line.split()}) for set in [set(line.split()) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:][:i]] for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:][i+1:]) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: No integer is used in more than one set (all sets are disjoint).
